_comment: Content that MUST stay Chinese in English / French. Each entry: text (regex on the string), sel (regex on the element path), route (regex on the route), kind (text / userbox / attr:...), reason. An entry needs at least one of text / sel / route.

allow.reason: The language menu names every language in its own script (中文 / English / Français), so that a user who cannot read the current language finds theirs.
Quotes the exact label that the user's Chinese Google / Excel sheet must contain in column A (the import reads this Chinese pattern); an example in another language would not be recognised.

Classical poems are the thing being studied: titles, poets, dynasties, the lines themselves and their word notes are Chinese literature shown in Chinese (the screens around them are translated). OPEN QUESTION for the user: the one-sentence gists and word notes could get EN/FR translations (about 185 gists and 700 notes).

The labels on the map of China name the provinces, seas and islands in Chinese, as on a Chinese school map; the information card next to the map gives the English / French name, the abbreviation and the pinyin.
The times-table rhyme (乘法口诀, for example 三四十二) is the Chinese text that is spoken and learned; the English / French line under it explains the product.
The heading of an element card is the Chinese element name next to the English name (the Chinese character is what a Chinese textbook uses).
The element's Chinese character in the periodic-table cell (氢, 氦 ...): the table is the Chinese school table; the tooltip and the card give the English name.

KNOWN GAP (open question): the task statements, hints, lessons and level titles of the text-coding worlds 11-13 and the workshop templates are Chinese content in user boxes by the design of rule 61 (about 340 + 80 strings, none translated yet).

KNOWN GAP (open question): the lessons, scenario cards, sort cards and hints of the information-technology worlds 14-16 are Chinese content in user boxes by the design of rule 62 (about 600 strings in coding-info.json, none translated yet).
Program text: string literals and comments inside the example Python programs of the text-coding lessons and workshop (the program prints exactly this text; the level checks compare it).

The characters on the Chinese-chess (xiangqi) pieces (车 马 象 士 将 炮 卒 ...) and the river legend 楚河 汉界 are part of the real game's pieces and board; the screens, messages and move names around them are translated.
A string literal in the example Python program of a text-coding lesson (the lesson's demo prints this Chinese text, as the task asks).
